extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by professional translators. It enables the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual machine translation systems.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal; Cynthia Gao; Vishrav Chaudhary; Peng-Jen Chen; Guillaume Wenzek; Da Ju; Sanjana Krishnan; Marc’Aurelio Ranzato; Francisco Guzmán; Angela Fan

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia by randomly selecting articles from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage, and having 10 annotators manually select 3 to 5 contiguous sentences from each article. These sentences were then professionally translated into 101 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles sourced specifically from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by professional translators through a translation Language Service Provider (LSP), edited by different translators within the LSP, and then evaluated by an independent evaluation LSP to determine a Translation Quality Score based on error types and severity, with a 90% acceptance threshold.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: An independent evaluation LSP assessed quality by tallying errors (such as grammar, mistranslation, and unnatural translation) and their severity (minor, major, critical) to calculate a Translation Quality Score on a 0 to 100 scale. Translations scoring below 90% were sent back for re-translation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 6 male; 4 female; researchers (scientists and engineers); program/project managers; East Asia; South Asia; Southern Europe; Latin America; North America
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Source sentences not in English are produced by human translators, which may introduce translationese (overly literal or awkward translations).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The majority of the world's population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages; evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems; document-level translation; multimodal translation; sentence and document classification; language identification; multilingual domain adaptation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were manually selected to avoid segments with very short or malformed sentences. Translations were filtered using automatic checks including language identification, length difference checks, fluency checks via a language model, and a heuristic to detect and reject translations that were likely copies from commercial translation engines.
